BUS.G11.T1.CHALLENGES.A1.title: Challenges of the micro, market and macro environments
BUS.G11.T1.CHALLENGES.A1.description: Identifying the challenges of each environment: micro (difficult employees, weak vision, poor management, strikes), market (competition, supply shortages, changing consumer behaviour) and macro (legislation, income changes, globalisation, socio-economic issues).
BUS.G11.T1.CHALLENGES.A1.strand: T1 — Business environments, socio-economic issues, sectors, ownership & acquiring a business
BUS.G11.T1.CHALLENGES.A1.recovery_strategy: Sort a challenge by where it comes from: inside the business = micro (staff, vision, management); close outside = market (competitors, suppliers, customers); broad outside = macro (laws, economy, globalisation).

questions.question: A lack of vision and difficult employees are challenges of which environment?
questions.expected: The micro (internal) environment
questions.memo: Vision and employees are inside the business, so problems with them are micro-environment challenges.

questions.question: Strong competition and supply shortages are challenges of which environment?
questions.expected: The market environment
questions.memo: Competitors and suppliers are part of the market environment, so problems with them are market-environment challenges.

questions.question: True or false: New legislation and globalisation are challenges of the macro environment.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Laws and globalisation are broad outside forces, which makes them macro-environment challenges.

questions.question: A strike by the business's own workers is a challenge of the _________ environment.
questions.expected: micro
questions.memo: The workers are inside the business, so a strike by them is a micro-environment challenge.

questions.question: Which of these is a market-environment challenge?
options: A change in consumer buying behaviour
A rise in the national inflation rate
questions.expected: A change in consumer buying behaviour
questions.memo: Consumers are part of the market environment. A demotivated workforce and weak mission are micro; inflation is macro.

questions.question: True or false: A supplier running out of stock is a micro-environment challenge.
questions.expected: False
questions.memo: A supplier is part of the market environment, so a supply shortage is a market-environment challenge, not a micro one.

questions.question: Sort each challenge into the environment it belongs to.

items.text: Managers who lack the right skills
A supplier who cannot deliver stock

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Inside the business = micro (staff, managers). Close outside = market (competitors, suppliers). Broad outside = macro (interest rates, laws).

questions.question: Read the case and select the MACRO-environment challenges it mentions.
questions.source_text: A furniture maker is under pressure. A new import tax has raised the price of its timber. The economy has slowed and customers are spending less. On top of this, two of its machine operators have resigned and its main competitor has dropped its prices.
questions.task: Tap the parts that describe macro-environment challenges (broad outside forces the business cannot control).

targets.phrase: A new import tax has raised the price of its timber
targets.reason: Taxes and laws are a legal/economic macro force.

targets.phrase: The economy has slowed and customers are spending less
targets.reason: A slowing economy is an economic macro force.

questions.expected: A new import tax has raised the price of its timber; The economy has slowed and customers are spending less
questions.memo: The import tax and the slowing economy are macro forces. The resigning operators are a micro challenge; the competitor's price drop is a market challenge.

questions.question: Why is competition treated as a MARKET challenge rather than a macro one?
options: Competitors are specific firms close to the business, not a broad force affecting everyone
Competition only ever affects large businesses
Competition is controlled by the government
Competition has no effect on a business
questions.expected: Competitors are specific firms close to the business, not a broad force affecting everyone
questions.memo: Market challenges come from specific close parties (competitors, suppliers, customers). Macro challenges are broad forces like the economy or laws.

questions.question: Changes in income levels, political changes and globalisation are challenges of the _________ environment.
questions.expected: macro
questions.memo: Income levels, politics and globalisation are broad outside forces — macro-environment challenges.

questions.question: A business is struggling because its managers lack skills and its staff are demotivated. These are challenges of the _________ environment.
questions.expected: micro
questions.memo: Managers and staff are inside the business, so these are micro-environment challenges that management can act on directly.

questions.question: True or false: Changes in demographics and socio-cultural values can challenge a business through both its market and its macro environment.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Shifts in what specific customers want show up in the market environment, while broad social and demographic change is a macro force — both are challenges.

questions.question: Which best describes a macro-environment challenge?
options: A broad force, like the economy or new laws, that affects all businesses
The business choosing a new logo
questions.expected: A broad force, like the economy or new laws, that affects all businesses
questions.memo: Macro challenges are broad, society-wide forces. A single employee is micro; one supplier is market; a logo is an internal choice.

questions.question: Sort each challenge into the environment it belongs to.

items.text: Customers switching to a rival brand
A key supplier raising its prices

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Go-slows and a weak vision are inside (micro); customers and suppliers are close outside (market); a recession and import rules are broad outside (macro).

questions.question: A new minimum-wage law raises a factory's labour costs. This is a challenge of which environment?
questions.expected: The macro environment
questions.memo: Laws are part of the macro environment. The factory must adapt because it cannot control legislation.

questions.question: Read the case and select the MARKET-environment challenges it mentions.
questions.source_text: A bakery is battling on several fronts. Its head baker keeps arriving late. A bigger bakery has opened across the road and is undercutting its prices. Its flour supplier has run short and cannot deliver, while a new health regulation has forced it to upgrade its kitchen.
questions.task: Tap the parts that describe market-environment challenges (close outside parties the business deals with).

targets.phrase: A bigger bakery has opened across the road and is undercutting its prices
targets.reason: A competitor is part of the market environment.

targets.phrase: Its flour supplier has run short and cannot deliver
targets.reason: A supplier is part of the market environment.

questions.expected: A bigger bakery has opened across the road and is undercutting its prices; Its flour supplier has run short and cannot deliver
questions.memo: The rival bakery and the flour supplier are market challenges. The late head baker is micro; the new health regulation is macro.

questions.question: A company faces difficult unions inside the business and fierce competition outside it. How are these two challenges best classified?
options: The union issue is micro; the competition is market
The union issue is market; the competition is micro
questions.expected: The union issue is micro; the competition is market
questions.memo: Unions and staff sit inside the business (micro); competitors sit close outside (market). Classifying them correctly shapes how the business responds.

questions.question: Why does it matter whether a challenge is micro, market or macro?
options: Because the business has different levels of control over each, so its response must differ
Because only macro challenges are real
Because micro challenges can always be ignored
Because the classification changes the law
questions.expected: Because the business has different levels of control over each, so its response must differ
questions.memo: A micro challenge can be fixed directly, a market challenge influenced, and a macro challenge only adapted to. Knowing the type guides the response.

questions.question: Read the case and select ONLY the macro-environment challenges.
questions.source_text: A clothing factory reports its problems. Load-shedding from the national grid keeps halting production. A weaker rand has raised the cost of imported zips. Meanwhile, two sewing machines have broken down and a long-standing customer has placed a smaller order than usual.
questions.task: Tap only the macro-environment challenges (broad forces beyond the factory's control).

targets.phrase: Load-shedding from the national grid keeps halting production
targets.reason: The national power supply is a macro (institutional/economic) force.

targets.phrase: A weaker rand has raised the cost of imported zips
targets.reason: The exchange rate is an economic/international macro force.

questions.expected: Load-shedding from the national grid keeps halting production; A weaker rand has raised the cost of imported zips
questions.memo: Load-shedding and the weaker rand are macro forces. The broken machines are micro; the smaller customer order is a market challenge.

questions.question: A business lists 'go-slows by staff' as a market-environment challenge. Why is this wrong?
options: Staff are inside the business, so a go-slow is a micro challenge
Go-slows are not challenges at all
Staff are part of the macro environment
questions.expected: Staff are inside the business, so a go-slow is a micro challenge
questions.memo: A go-slow comes from the business's own workers, who are inside the business — that makes it a micro-environment challenge.
